belief: If people really knew me, they would leave.
origins: If we have been rejected after being honest, shamed for a mistake, or teased for being vulnerable, we learn to hide. We show a polished version and keep the rest locked away. The result is lonely: people like the mask, and we are convinced they would reject the person behind it.
teaches: The psalmist says, “O LORD, You have searched me and known me. You know when I sit and when I rise; You understand my thoughts from afar.” God knows everything about you and has not left. Paul writes, “God proves His love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” John says, “If we walk in the light as He is in the light, we have fellowship with one another.” Being known, and still loved, is the heart of real fellowship. Not everyone is safe, but the right people can receive the real you.
self_statements: If they saw the real me, they would be disgusted.
I have to keep my guard up.
My past would scare them off.
They like me only because they do not know me.
No one could love all of me.
I must never let anyone see my weaknesses.
errors: Assuming I know how others would react.
Feeling ashamed and concluding that I am shameful.
Believing I must reveal everything or nothing.
questions: What am I most afraid people would discover?
Has anyone ever known something hard about me and stayed?
What is the cost of hiding?
Who is a safe person I could tell a little more?
What does it mean that God already knows me completely?
What small, safe disclosure could I try?
truth: God knows everything about me and loves me. I do not have to be perfect to be loved. With wise, safe people, I can let myself be known little by little and discover real acceptance.
hw_truths: God knows me completely and loves me.
Christ died for me at my worst.
log: Each week, record one small disclosure and how the person responded.
actions: Write what you are afraid they would discover.
Pick a trustworthy friend, pastor, or counselor.
Disclose something modest and notice the response.
Thank God that you are fully known and loved.
prayer: Lord, You know me completely and have not left. Give me courage to let safe people see more of me. Heal my fear of being rejected, and lead me to people who receive me with grace. Amen.
hw_questions: What do I fear they would learn?
What does it mean that God knows me?
name_example: Sarah can write: “God knows me completely and has not left, so I can let safe people know me.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “If people really knew me, they would leave.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
